Subject: Draft: GPU fleet scenarios & fallback ladder for Solace Health (S-2247)

Lena / Thomas —

Quick note following our call this morning. Attached is the spreadsheet with three capacity scenarios (Conservative, Target, Aggressive) and a short visual of the proposed fallback ladder. High-level asks from Solace that matter for sizing:

- Peak inference concurrency for EHR summarization: 250 concurrent sessions (95th pctl)
- Median session length ~3.2s per request, typical prompt length 600 tokens, expected growth to 1,000 tokens in Q2 post-launch
- Data residency: US-only; encryption at rest with customer KMS for Private and dedicated encryption for Dedicated Mode
- Procurement window: Solace needs procurement approval by Nov 30; deployment start by Jan 10 to meet their product launch

Initial capacity candidates in the sheet: A100_80GB slabs for Dedicated, H100_80GB for aggressive committed pool, and a Private on-prem baseline for the SOC2-bound queues. Key differences called out in the notes column: latency SLOs, lead times (30–60 days for dedicated reserved vs ~90–120 days for private appliance procurement + on-prem procurement), and failure modes.

Next step: internal alignment on which scenario we can commit to in the deal language (e.g., reserved QPS vs committed GPU count) and a short fallback ladder for when dedicated pool is saturated. Rishi — can you confirm the cost deltas and what net unit economics look like if Solace opts for the Target vs Aggressive slab for months 1–6? Karthik — can you double-check the procurement notes about APN marketplace timelines and whether we can accelerate a Dedicated region-side allocation? Marcus / Marissa — any compliance evidence gaps to flag before we share the security PDF?

I'll consolidate edits and share a clean version for SOW language by Friday.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Deals — Redwood Inference

Naomi — thanks for the doc. A few clarifications from our end:

1) The 250 concurrent sessions number is conservative — it's the launch goal. We expect 400 concurrent by end of Q2. Can you add a throughput stress row for +60%?
2) Latency target is p95 < 600ms for short prompts; for long prompts (1k tokens) p95 < 1.2s. Will dedicated vs private materially affect those numbers?
3) Procurement: we can sign a commitment but prefer language that lets us defer part of the committed pool until launch +90 days (staged commit). Is staged commit feasible?

Also, our security team will need an explicit statement about access controls for KV/prefix caches; they must not persist customer PHI outside the US. Attached is the security checklist we referenced.

Subject: Re: Draft: GPU fleet scenarios & fallback ladder for Solace Health (S-2247)

Folks — I pulled the numbers and added an extra stress column (+60%) into the sheet. Summary:

- Conservative: 6x A100_80GB reserved nodes (tile = 4 shards per node for our serving layout), expected to support ~180 concurrent short-session QPS at p95. Cost baseline: $X/hr per node (see sheet). Lead time: ready in ~30 days if we have a committed purchase.

- Target: 10x A100_80GB reserved nodes + 2x H100 burst nodes (spot-backed for short bursts). Supports ~320 concurrent short-session QPS at p95, headroom for 400 after batch optimizations and quantization. Cost uplift ~+45% vs Conservative.

- Aggressive: 14x H100_80GB dedicated (mixed quantized runtime), target for 400+ sustained concurrent QPS. Lead time for aggressive reserved procurement ~45–60 days. Significant cost increase but best latency headroom.

Important operational notes:
- Fallback ladder (proposed):
  1) Route traffic to dedicated pool (committed)
  2) If committed pool >85% utilized, auto-failover to compatible quantized model variants in Dedicated (lower token cost, slightly higher latency)
  3) If dedicated pool saturated, burst to shared-hosted fallback in the same region (no PHI persisted; strip or redirect PHI-containing traffic to Private on-prem queue)
  4) As last resort, degrade to summary-only mode (drop long-form generations) with explicit client-side flagging to maintain SLOs

- Private on-prem path: procurement + infra prep estimated 90–120 days; good for strict PHI handling and control, but not for short procurement timelines. We can sign a hybrid contract: guaranteed Dedicated pool for X months + option to deploy Private later with a credit toward hardware purchase.

Rishi — I've left placeholders for per-hour pricing and the suggested contract language around staged commit.

Karthik

On Mon, Nov 7, 2027 at 12:27 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — I pulled the numbers and added an extra stress column (+60%) into the sheet. Summary:
> 
> - Conservative: 6x A100_80GB reserved nodes ...
> - Target: 10x A100_80GB reserved nodes + 2x H100 burst nodes ...
> - Aggressive: 14x H100_80GB dedicated ...

Nice summary. A couple of specific numbers and contract asks to propose back to Solace:

1) Staged commit language (proposal):
   - Month 1–3: Customer pays for 60% of Target reserved capacity (billed monthly).
   - Month 4–6: Automatic ramp to 100% of Target unless either side gives 30-day written notice. Option to accelerate to Aggressive with a 60-day notice and prorated pricing adjustment.

2) SLA / credits tie-breaker: If the dedicated pool falls below the agreed throughput for >2 contiguous hours and fallback to shared-hosted was required, Redwood provides a credit equal to 5% of monthly committed fees per incident (cap 20% / month). This is an easier ask than immediate refunds and preserves our right to require staged provisioning.

3) Pricing sensitivity: the incremental cost to move from Target -> Aggressive is large; for large deals we should trade a modest committed discount (5–8%) for a longer-term commit (12+ months) rather than deeper discounts for 6-month terms.

4) Compliance gating: we must provide a short attestation that KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and not written to external long-term storage; will need Security to sign off on one-pager. Marissa / Marcus — can you produce that attestation by EOD Thursday?

I'll draft the short SOW paragraph and the staged commit clause. Naomi — once we agree internally I'll share a version to Solace with the three scenarios clearly numbered and the fallback ladder as a contract exhibit.

Rishi
